explanation: Build subsets in increasing order, choosing the next value strictly after the previous one. Bound each loop so enough values remain to finish the subset. Copy a completed subset into the output; k=0 produces one empty subset.
timeComplexity: O(k·C(n,k)) for nonempty subsets Each completed subset copies k elements; remaining-count pruning avoids branches that cannot finish.
spaceComplexity: O(k) auxiliary, plus O(k·C(n,k)) output Recursion retains at most k choices; the output stores k entries for each of C(n,k) subsets.
attribution: Unmodified reference source: epi_judge_cpp_solutions/combinations.cc. Elements of Programming Interviews Judge authors; repository LICENSE: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 International. Explanation authored for EPI Practice.
correctness: The chosen list is strictly increasing, so every recorded list is a k-element subset with no repetitions. Every subset has a unique sequence of next choices, and the remaining-count bound removes only branches that cannot reach size k.
walkthrough: For n=4,k=2, choosing first value 1 yields [1,2],[1,3],[1,4]; first value 2 yields [2,3],[2,4]; first value 3 yields [3,4]. These are all six subsets.
edgeCases: Only output order is unrestricted; each subset’s values are increasing.
